### ex-the-cardinality-of-the-continuum — REFUSE
CURRENT TEXT READ: "[L7] For a well-orderable set $X$, $\lvert X\rvert$ is the least ordinal equinumerous with $X$ and equinumerous sets receive the same one ([[lem-cardinality-of-a-well-orderable-set]], [[def-cardinal]]); assuming the Axiom of Choice every set has one ([[thm-well-ordering-theorem]])." / "[L1] $\mathbb{R}$ is a complete ordered field with a total order ([[def-real-numbers]], [[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-real-order]]), hence Archimedean ([[thm-of-archimedean]]), and $\iota : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}$ is the unique order-preserving field embedding ([[lem-of-q-embeds]])."
ASSESSMENT: The L7 repair is correct: lem-cardinality-of-a-well-orderable-set gives the least equinumerous ordinal for a well-orderable set, def-cardinal defines the resulting initial ordinal, and thm-well-ordering-theorem says “Assume the Axiom of Choice. Then every set X can be well ordered.” But L1 remains a fatal dependency-citation defect. def-real-numbers says only “The real numbers are the quotient ring” of Cauchy sequences by null sequences. def-real-order defines positivity and the relation. def-complete-ordered-field defines what completeness means for an already ordered field. None states that this constructed real system is totally ordered or complete. The missing targets state exactly what is needed: thm-reals-ordered-field says the published relation “makes R a totally ordered field,” and cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete says the Cauchy-sequence reals “have the least-upper-bound property.” Since thm-of-archimedean assumes a complete ordered field, it cannot supply its own unmet hypothesis. Thus L1 and its uses are not licensed by the declared dependencies.
COLLATERAL: the L7 repair itself broke nothing; the separate load-bearing L1 citation defect remains unresolved

### ex-the-cofinality-of-aleph-omega — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "[L5] For a well-orderable set $X$, $\lvert X\rvert$ is the least ordinal equinumerous with $X$, and equinumerous sets receive the same one ([[lem-cardinality-of-a-well-orderable-set]], [[def-equinumerous]])." / "[L6] Ordinals satisfy trichotomy, $\alpha \subseteq \beta$ iff $\alpha \in \beta$ or $\alpha = \beta$, and $\alpha \subseteq \beta \subseteq \alpha$ forces $\alpha = \beta$ ([[lem-ordinal-trichotomy]], [[lem-ordinal-basics]])."
ASSESSMENT: Correct. lem-cardinality-of-a-well-orderable-set says that a well-orderable X has a least equinumerous ordinal and that equinumerous well-orderable sets receive the same cardinal; def-equinumerous says equinumerous means that a bijection exists. lem-ordinal-trichotomy says exactly one membership direction or equality holds, while lem-ordinal-basics states the equivalence between ordinal inclusion and membership-or-equality. These license L5 and L6. Removing the injection-definition citation was correct because L6 uses only ordinal comparison. The range of the strictly increasing map from omega is cofinal, has cardinality aleph zero, and the lower bound follows from cofinality being an infinite cardinal.

### ex-a-singular-cardinal-of-uncountable-cofinality — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "[L7] For a well-orderable set $X$, $\lvert X\rvert$ is the least ordinal equinumerous with $X$, equinumerous sets receive the same one, and $\lvert \alpha\rvert = \alpha$ exactly when $\alpha$ is a cardinal ([[lem-cardinality-of-a-well-orderable-set]], [[def-cardinal]], [[def-equinumerous]])." / "[L9] Ordinals satisfy trichotomy; $\alpha \subseteq \beta$ iff $\alpha \in \beta$ or $\alpha = \beta$; the union of a set of ordinals is its least upper bound; every nonempty set of ordinals has an $\in$-least element; and every strictly increasing map of ordinals is injective ([[lem-ordinal-trichotomy]], [[lem-ordinal-basics]], [[def-injection-surjection-bijection]])."
ASSESSMENT: Correct. The cardinality lemma gives the least equinumerous ordinal, invariance under equinumerosity, and the exact cardinal criterion; def-cardinal and def-equinumerous supply those terms. lem-ordinal-trichotomy gives trichotomy and least elements, lem-ordinal-basics gives the union and inclusion clauses, and def-injection-surjection-bijection says a map is injective when equality of values forces equality of inputs. Strict increase therefore implies injectivity in one line. The lower-bound argument is valid: thm-countable-subsets-of-omega-one-are-bounded says, under countable choice, every at-most-countable subset of omega one is bounded there; thm-cofinality-basics says cofinality of a limit ordinal is an infinite cardinal. These yield cofinality exactly aleph one.

### ex-an-aleph-fixed-point — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "The power operation behaves differently: assuming the Axiom of Choice, so that $2^{\kappa}$ is a cardinal at all, $\kappa < 2^{\kappa}$ at every cardinal ([[thm-cardinal-power-set-and-cantor]]), so there are no fixed points there at all. That comparison is an aside; nothing below uses it, and the example itself stays in ZF." / "[L7] An injective map onto its range is a bijection to that range; for a well-orderable set $X$, $\lvert X\rvert$ is the least ordinal equinumerous with $X$, and equinumerous sets receive the same cardinal ([[def-injection-surjection-bijection]], [[lem-cardinality-of-a-well-orderable-set]], [[def-equinumerous]])." / "So this fixed point is singular, and, assuming the Axiom of Choice, by [[cor-cofinality-of-a-cardinal-power]] it is therefore not a possible value of $2^{\aleph_0}$."
ASSESSMENT: Correct. thm-cardinal-power-set-and-cantor begins “Assume the Axiom of Choice” and states that every cardinal is strictly below its power-set cardinal. cor-cofinality-of-a-cardinal-power also begins with that hypothesis and states that the cofinality of the continuum is greater than aleph zero. Both repaired qualifications are therefore exact. def-injection-surjection-bijection defines injectivity and surjectivity, so an injective map viewed with its range as codomain is immediately bijective; the cardinality lemma then supplies the cardinal of that range. The tower is strictly increasing, its supremum is a limit, continuity gives the fixed-point equation, and its countable cofinal range gives cofinality aleph zero.

ASSESSMENT: Correct. def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies says “The beths, assuming the Axiom of Choice, are the parallel operation” and gives the base, successor, and limit clauses; the hierarchy corollary gives infinite cardinal values, strict increase, and continuity. The repaired title now matches that hypothesis. The cardinality lemma, def-cardinal, and def-equinumerous license L4, while thm-well-ordering-theorem says every set can be well ordered under choice. The omega lemma says omega is a limit ordinal; the ordinal lemmas give trichotomy, unions, and comparison; the injection definition makes strict increase imply injectivity immediately. The first three beth values and the cofinality calculation follow correctly.
